column1: # Stops proven unreachable: path, message, file:symbol of the check that rules the stop out, reason.
# Tools/Agent/PanicRatchet.jet checks every row; see PROVEN there.

column2: the lambda's row node left the graph
column4: It pops the lambda node it pushed. The walk between them only reads and writes nodes by index: it pushes nothing it does not pop (this function is the only push onto a walk's node list), and nothing removes a node.

column2: the region node left the local list
column4: The region's walk starts from a list holding the region node alone. The only push onto a walk's node list is this function's, which pops its node again, and nothing removes a node, so the walk ends with the region node still in place.

column2: a collected effect node left its unit
column4: The unit's collection starts from a list holding the unit's node alone. The only push onto a walk's node list is this function's, which pops its node again, and nothing removes a node, so the collection ends with the unit's node still in place.

column2: compiler-owned enum has no variant menu
column4: The loop names Ordering, RemoveBy and TaskPauseMode, which this table gives non-empty literal menus, and UnitScaleProvenanceKind, which sema_fact_enum_variants beside it gives a non-empty literal menu. No name reaches the lookup from a program.

column2: an accepted body packet has no checked result
column4: A packet comes from one of four places. Three build it with `checked: Val(...)`: sema_check_prepare_method_body, sema_check_body_claimed_top_level and sema_core_body_capture. The fourth is the Core bodies file, and every packet read from it, directly or read ahead, passes this decode, which refuses a packet with no result. `checked` is taken out only in sema_check_drain_body and sema_check_registration_method, and each drops the packet afterward.

column2: a finishing stream module's environment has no module scope
column4: A stream module's cell starts empty, and an environment enters it only through sema_check_body_stream_enter, from the list this function returns. That list is either empty or holds the one environment whose module_scope this function sets to Val. Only two takers clear module_scope, sema_check_body_stream_take_environment and sema_check_body_stream_take_scope, and each does so after moving the environment out of the cell.

column2: a stream module's environment has no module scope to copy
column4: The copy reads an environment held in a stream module's cell; sema_check_body_stream_enter's call is guarded by `module_scope != None`. A cell gets environments only from the list this function returns, whose one environment has module_scope set to Val. The two takers clear module_scope only after moving the environment out of the cell.

column2: a done stream module's environment has no module scope
column4: A stream module's cell starts empty, and an environment enters it only through sema_check_body_stream_enter, from the list this function returns. That list is either empty or holds the one environment whose module_scope this function sets to Val. Only two takers clear module_scope, sema_check_body_stream_take_environment and sema_check_body_stream_take_scope, and each does so after moving the environment out of the cell.

column2: the shared environment gave back no module scope
column4: This function is the only caller of sema_check_shared_lend_scope and sema_check_shared_return_scope. It lends the scope (module_scope = Val) before its threads start and takes it back only after they join. Both of its callers hold the pass's shared state alone for the whole call, and the threads only read it.

column2: the shared environment lent a thread no module scope
column4: sema_check_body_part_copy_scope runs only on the threads of sema_check_body_parts, which only this function calls, between its sema_check_shared_lend_scope (module_scope = Val) and its sema_check_shared_return_scope. The threads read the shared environment through guard_read and never write it.

column2: body publication lost its authenticated item frontier
column4: The publish's one compiler caller is jet_driver_comptime_apply_landed, which only this function calls, always with its run's environment, its `values` and `from` = resolved_count. jet_driver_run_comptime makes that environment with sema_comptime_environment, which sets item_frontier to the length of the initial values; the run starts `values` as their copy and resolved_count at its length. `values` only grows (push), each call runs only when values.len() > resolved_count, and each sets item_frontier to values.len() while resolved_count is set to values.len() after it. The environment only moves through the precheck threads' shared state and back, and nothing else writes item_frontier or replaces the run environment's publication.

column2: the IR optimizer has no body for function {id}
column4: ir_opt_inline_marked_module pushes one body onto bodies[id] for each marked id, and starts this walk only at marked ids; the walk recurses only into marked callees and only from state 0, and pushes each id it walks once, so marked_order holds marked ids, each once. ir_opt_inline_build only reads `bodies`, and each pass of the loop pops bodies[id] and pushes its one result back, so bodies[id] holds one body when its turn comes.

column2: symbol id out of range
column4: Every SymbolKeys comes from this constructor or symbol_keys_empty (0, 0), and only three callers make one: symbol_builtin_keys_build (0, SYMBOL_LOCAL_BOUND, then bound lowered to its key count), symbol_table_of's open range (end, SYMBOL_LOCAL_BOUND - end) and sema_registration_prepare_graph's module ranges, consecutive from the builtin range's end within three quarters of the ids left below SYMBOL_LOCAL_BOUND. So base >= 0 and base + bound <= SYMBOL_LOCAL_BOUND (2^31 - 1), and the line before refuses row >= bound, so base + row < 2^31 fits a U32.

column2: symbol range at {range.base} overlaps the range before it, which ends at {end}
column4: symbol_table_of's callers outside tests are symbol_table and sema_registration_graph_snapshot, each with the builtin range alone, and this function. Its module ranges start at the builtin range's end (the builtin range is base 0) and each starts where the one before ends; every bound is a non-negative share (weights are positive), and a duplicate module's range is dropped, not added. Interning never moves a range's base or bound.

column2: body publication attempted to append through an old prefix generation
column4: The one compiler path to this append is sema_comptime_body_values_append_items from sema_comptime_environment_publish_body_values, on the staging run's environment, whose publication this function makes with sema_comptime_body_values_freeze: fresh facts holding `length` rows. Facts rows are pushed only by this append, under the facts guard, and the publication's length is then set to the facts' row count; truncation and prefixes write a context's view or a new value, never this publication, and the environments that share its facts by copy never publish.

column2: a body prefix lost its facts owner
column4: A SemaComptimeBodyValues starts with facts None and length 0 (its field defaults), or comes from this function, which gives facts whenever length is not 0. Facts are only ever replaced by Val (the line after this stop), length is raised only after that (sema_comptime_body_values_append_items) and otherwise only lowered (sema_comptime_body_values_truncate, sema_comptime_body_values_prefix). So facts None means length 0.

column2: body publication has no facts owner
column4: The lines just before this one set publication.facts to Val when it is None, and nothing between them and this read changes it.

column2: the authenticated body frontier contained no new body row
column4: The one compiler call of sema_comptime_body_values_append_items is in sema_comptime_environment_publish_body_values, only when body_values_changed, which only this function calls. It sets body_values_changed only when values[from..] holds a BodyExpression row, and passes the same `values` and `from` on; the append counts each BodyExpression row in values[from..], so it counts at least one.

column2: the codec trait `{reference.name}` is not an owned trait
column4: sema_registration_compiler_owned_codec_trait's one caller is this function, whose loop passes builtin_codec_trait_ref of .Encode and .Decode, which name "Encode" and "Decode" (builtin_codec_trait_name). OWNED_TRAITS holds a row of each name (OwnedTraitRows.jet), so symbol_builtin finds one, and its id, 1 plus the row's index, fits a U32.

column2: a prepared module lost its symbol range
column4: The table this function makes holds exactly the job's one range. A table's ranges are only pushed in symbol_table_of and never popped or replaced anywhere else: interning writes into the last range, and sema_registration_prepare_module_row only interns through it. So the pop finds that range.

column2: the module import `{declaration.alias}` of `{source_text}` has no symbol (sema_registration_mint_module_imports)
column4: sema_registration_populate_imports has one caller, this function's loop, which runs after its loop minting every module's imports with sema_registration_mint_module_imports. All sema_registration_add_import calls come earlier in this function. The mint interns the Import key of the module's identity text, the import's target identity text and its alias for every non-Unqualified import, and this stop is in the File/Module branch and reads the same import (target_module_identity, declaration.alias) of the same module. In between, the graph's symbols only grow by interning.

column2: the precheck scopes lost the slot they prepared
column4: Both callers (sema_comptime_precheck_enter_one, sema_comptime_precheck_enter) pass scopes made by this function, which hold one slot, after sema_comptime_scopes_prepare, and only once `kept` has read slots[current]. Prepare either replaces the list with one slot (a snapshot graph), writes a slot in place, or pushes one; it never removes a slot. So the list is not empty.

column2: the precheck module scope left its module environment
column4: The one caller of sema_comptime_precheck_thread_scopes passes module_environments[current]. Every environment pushed onto module_environments has just been given module_scope = Val by this function: directly in sema_comptime_precheck_enter, or through sema_comptime_precheck_enter_one's kept environment in sema_comptime_precheck_enter_store. The list is otherwise only emptied and read under the shared guard, and nothing writes module_scope of an environment in it.

column2: a comptime walk scope was dropped while a job of it was queued
column4: A job is claimed only while unclaimed and only when its slot is in state 2: from `order`, which receives a job only when its slot is in state 2 (sema_comptime_walk_push, sema_comptime_walk_install_slot), or from the preferred slot's queue, which is checked for state 2. Entering state 2 sets slots[slot] to Val. pending[slot] counts the slot's unclaimed jobs. This function, the only one that sets a slot to None, does so only when pending is 0 and the slot is not in the push's `keep`. It also unmaps the slot's module, so no later push queues a job on it.

column2: {ir_type_name(ty)} has no row
column4: Every compiler call of ir_scalar_type_row passes a literal Type.Int, Type.Bool, Type.Float, Type.String or Type.IntN of 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits (the one other argument, U8 in OptVersion.jet, is in a #Test). This function gives Val for each: a cached scalar row, else a layout for Int, Bool, Float and String, and for an IntN of at most 64 bits whose type_id_well_known id is not none, which those four widths have in both signs.

column2: the merge has {preps.len()} part preparations for {parts.len()} parts
column4: ir_merge_new's one caller is ir_merge_with, called by ir_merge (from ir_merge_serial, one part and its one preparation, and a #Test) and by ir_build_waves_finish with ir_build_waves_parted's lists. Those gather every slot's modules and preps; each slot is made holding one module and no prep, nothing else pushes or pops a slot's modules or preps, and this function runs ir_wave_glues once on every slot, which pushes the one prep of its module. So both lists have one row per slot.

column2: a settled foreign closure node lost its check
column4: This arm runs only when `settled_foreign`, computed a few lines above as index.nodes[node].settled && index.nodes[node].foreign != None; nothing in between writes the node (the memory plan only reads the program), so `foreign` is still Val.

column2: a wait-cycle path lost its key
column4: A call that reaches this pop pushed its own key onto `path` first; it returns before the push only from the two early checks. Each nested call either returns true, which makes this call return true at once without reaching the pop, or returns false, having popped exactly the key it pushed (or pushed none). So the top of `path` here is this call's key.

column2: the run's symbol table left core reachability
column4: The caller hands it `symbol_rows` holding one table, made just before. This function either returns before touching the list (no Core module) or moves the list's rows into its shared slot, whose threads only read symbols[0], and transfers them all back before it returns. So the list holds its one row again at the pop.

column2: the run's interner left core reachability
column4: The caller hands it `interner_rows` holding one interner, made just before. This function either returns before touching the list (no Core module) or moves the list's rows into its shared slot, whose threads only read interners[0], and transfers them all back before it returns. So the list holds its one row again at the pop.

column2: the state's argument was bound above
column4: The call has exactly params.len() arguments, each given a slot in 0..<params.len() that no earlier argument took (or the call is rejected), so the slots cover every parameter. The loop over the arguments sets locals[slot] to Val for each, or returns, so locals[state_slot] is Val after it.

column2: each argument was bound above
column4: sema_app_notify_call's one caller is this function, passing its `locals` after the argument loop. The call has exactly params.len() arguments, each given a slot in 0..<params.len() that no earlier argument took (or the call is rejected), so the slots cover every parameter, and the loop sets locals[slot] to Val for each, or returns. So every row of `locals` is Val.

column2: a helper marked failed has no message
column4: Its callers ask only for a key whose memo reads -2. A -2 is written only by the close glue builders (BuildMaps.jet ir_map_rest_glue, BuildOwn.jet twice) into close_glue and by the record and render helper builders (BuildTypes.jet) through ir_function_bind, each followed at once by this function for the same key, which records the message. ir_module_drop_build_memos clears close_glue together with the messages; it keeps function_rows, but it runs on a part only after the part's last build, and the merge binds only ids of 0 and up into a fresh module.

column2: comptime seccomp layout: the cookie check ends at {rest}, the program has {program.len()} instructions
column4: Straight-line count: the block pushes 7 instructions, one per file call, then 5, so it ends at start + 12 + calls.len(), and `rest` is start + 7 + calls.len() + 1 + 2 + 1 + 1, the same index.

column2: comptime seccomp layout: allow is {allow}, the program has {program.len()} instructions
column4: Straight-line count: the block pushes 4 instructions, one per allowed call, 1, 3, 1, one per descriptor, then 2, so it ends at start + 11 + allowed.len() + fds.len(), and `allow` is start + 4 + allowed.len() + 1 + 3 + 1 + fds.len() + 1, one less.

column2: comptime seccomp jump out of range at {at}
column4: x64_comptime_bpf_bytes's one caller is this function. Its program's jump targets depend only on the constant call lists and `stdout` (the cookie sets only `k` fields), every target is a later instruction, and the #Test beside it encodes the program with and without standard output, so every program it can build encodes with each jump in 0..255.

column2: the comptime seccomp program runs off its end
column4: x64_comptime_bpf_run is called only from #Test blocks, each on a program this function built. Its last instruction is a RET_K (the refusal block's allow), every jump lands on a later instruction inside the program (x64_comptime_bpf_bytes), and the run steps forward from 0, so it reaches a RET_K before it passes the end.

column2: HTTP mux route handler is neither a lambda nor a named function
column4: sema_http_mux_route_handler's one caller is this function, which passes the handler expression it gave sema_http_route_shape and rejects the call (E2805) when that returns None; nothing between them changes the expression. sema_http_route_shape returns a shape only for a lambda or an identifier, possibly in parentheses, and sema_http_mux_lambda and sema_http_mux_callee accept exactly those forms, so a handler that is not a lambda has a callee.

column2: checked Authority wire row is missing
column4: CORE_CALLS is built while the compiler builds (#run core_call_rows) from the dispatcher rows followed by every CORE_CALL_EXTENSIONS row, and that table declares the plain (no receiver) `core.plugin.__authority_to_wire` row; a key that would repeat refuses the build, and core_call looks keys up in CORE_CALL_KEYS, built from CORE_CALLS. So the lookup finds the row in every compiler that builds.

column2: the CoreSource row `{owner}` {role} is checked as its source call
column4: sema_value_method_kind's two callers are this function, both after it returns sema_value_method_core_source for a row whose lowering is CoreSource, and nothing between them changes the row, so the kind is never asked of a CoreSource row.

column2: a walked nominal left no active key
column4: This function is the only code that pushes or pops `active_keys`: it pushes its key, walks the members (whose nested calls each push and pop one key, with no return between), and then pops, so the stack holds at least its own key at the pop. A walk is replaced only between walks, never inside one.

column2: the IR optimizer has no body for function {id}
column4: ir_opt_serial's one caller hands it the rows ir_opt_rows just made, one body in each row, and nothing else touches them until ir_opt_serial returns. Each pass of its loop pops bodies[id] and pushes its one result back, so every row holds one body whenever an id reaches it.
